Task: Write a comprehensive guide to making homemade sourdough bread.

Comprehensive Guide to Making Homemade Sourdough Bread
=====================================================

CONTENTS  
1. Introduction  
2. Equipment & Ingredients  
3. Step-by-Step Timeline (Example 2-Day Schedule)  
4. Creating & Maintaining a Starter  
5. The Dough Process  
 A. Planning Hydration & Formula  
 B. Autolyse  
 C. Mixing & Adding Salt  
 D. Bulk Fermentation  
 E. Folding / “Stretch-and-Folds”  
 F. Preshaping & Bench Rest  
 G. Final Shaping  
 H. Proofing (Cold vs. Room-Temperature)  
6. Scoring & Baking  
7. Post-Bake Care  
8. Troubleshooting Chart  
9. Flavor Variations & Add-Ins  
10. Frequently Asked Questions  

——————————————————————————————————
1. Introduction
——————————————————————————————————
Sourdough bread relies on naturally occurring wild yeast and lactic-acid bacteria (LAB) rather than commercial baker’s yeast. The yeast produces carbon dioxide for rise; LAB create mild acidity that extends shelf life and deepens flavor. Mastering sourdough involves:

• Healthy, active starter  
• Temperature control  
• Gluten development through hydration, time, and folds  
• Proper shaping and proofing  
• Steam and heat management in the oven  

——————————————————————————————————
2. Equipment & Ingredients
——————————————————————————————————
ESSENTIAL EQUIPMENT
• Digital kitchen scale (1-g precision)  
• Mixing bowl (glass or stainless)  
• Dough scraper and/or bowl scraper  
• Banneton basket or towel-lined colander  
• Dutch oven (cast iron) or baking stone + steam tray  
• Razor blade or lame for scoring  
• Instant-read thermometer (optional but helpful)  

NICE-TO-HAVE
• Proofing box or warm spot (≈24–26 °C / 75–79 °F)  
• Bench knife for shaping  
• Rice flour to dust bannetons (prevents sticking)  
• Probe thermometer for dough  

CORE INGREDIENTS
1. Flour  
 • Strong bread flour (11.5–13 % protein) for structure  
 • Whole-grain flour (whole wheat or rye) for flavor & nutrients  
2. Water (preferably filtered; 20–25 °C / 68–77 °F)  
3. Salt (2 % of total flour weight)  
4. Mature sourdough starter (20–30 % of total flour weight in a typical “levain”)  

——————————————————————————————————
3. Step-by-Step Timeline (Example 2-Day Schedule)
——————————————————————————————————
DAY 1  
07:00 Feed starter (1 : 1 : 1 ratio of starter : water : flour)  
13:00 Build levain (larger pre-ferment)  
17:00 Autolyse flour + water (30 min–2 h)  
19:00 Mix in levain & salt → Begin bulk fermentation  
19:30 1st fold  
20:00 2nd fold  
20:30 3rd fold  
22:30 End bulk; preshape; bench rest 20 min  
23:00 Final shape; place in banneton; refrigerate 12–16 h  

DAY 2  
08:00 Preheat oven & Dutch oven to 250 °C / 480 °F (45 min)  
08:45 Score; bake 20 min covered + 20 min uncovered  
09:25 Cool on rack ≥1 h before slicing  

——————————————————————————————————
4. Creating & Maintaining a Starter
——————————————————————————————————
A. INITIAL BUILD (DAYS 1–7)  
Day 1 Mix 50 g whole-grain flour + 50 g water. Cover loosely, 25 °C/77 °F.  
Day 2 Should show bubbles; discard half; feed 50 g flour + 50 g water.  
Days 3–7 Repeat every 24 h (or 12 h if active). Switch to 50 % bread flour 50 % whole.  

Signs of readiness: doubles in 4–6 h, domed top, pleasant tangy smell, not overly sour/alcoholic.  

B. ONGOING MAINTENANCE  
• Daily feeding at room temp (1 : 2 : 2 starter : water : flour)  
• Or store in fridge; feed weekly, let sit 1 h, then refrigerate.  

——————————————————————————————————
5. The Dough Process
——————————————————————————————————
FORMULA EXAMPLE (makes one ~800 g loaf)  
• Bread flour 350 g  
• Whole-wheat flour 50 g  
• Water 300 g (75 % hydration)  
• Salt 8 g (2 %)  
• Levain 100 g (20 % of flour weight)  

Total dough weight ≈808 g. Adjust hydration for experience level.

A. Autolyse  
Combine flour + 280 g water (reserve 20 g for later). Rest 30 min–2 h. Purpose: hydrate starch, begin gluten development.

B. Mixing & Adding Salt  
Add levain; pinch & fold until incorporated. Rest 20 min. Dissolve salt in reserved 20 g water, mix until homogeneous.

C. Bulk Fermentation  
Target dough temp 24–26 °C (75–79 °F). Length 3–5 h depending on temperature & levain strength. Dough should rise 30–50 %, look puffier, domed edges.

D. Folds  
Perform 3–4 sets of stretch-and-folds every 30 min during first half of bulk. Lift one edge, stretch, fold over center, rotate bowl; repeat four sides.

E. Preshaping  
Lightly flour bench, turn out dough. Using scraper, gather into taut round. Rest 15–30 min uncovered.

F. Final Shaping  
Dust top of dough, flip. For boule: fold bottom up, sides to center, roll up, then drag to create surface tension. For batard: letter fold, roll, seal seam.

G. Proofing  
Place seam-up in floured banneton. Options:  
• Cold retard: 4–24 h at 4 °C/39 °F (enhances flavor, convenience).  
• Room temp: 1–2 h until dough slowly springs back when poked.  

H. Readiness Test  
Finger poke: indent should very slowly refill halfway. Over-proofed = no spring; under-proofed = quick rebound.

——————————————————————————————————
6. Scoring & Baking
——————————————————————————————————
1. Preheat Dutch oven at 250 °C / 480 °F for at least 40 min.  
2. Turn dough onto parchment. Brush off excess flour.  
3. Score 0.5–1 cm deep with swift, angled cut (classic “ear” = 30° angle along length).  
4. Transfer to Dutch oven. Cover; bake 20 min (steam phase).  
5. Remove lid; lower to 230 °C / 445 °F; bake 18–25 min until deep mahogany, internal temp 96–98 °C (205–208 °F).  
6. Cool minimum 1 h to set crumb.  

No Dutch oven? Bake on preheated stone; add steam by pouring hot water into tray at bottom during first 10 min.

——————————————————————————————————
7. Post-Bake Care
——————————————————————————————————
• Do not slice hot bread—steam escapes, gummy crumb forms.  
• Store cut-side down on board for 24 h, then in paper bag.  
• Freeze slices or whole loaf (well wrapped) up to 3 months; refresh in 180 °C oven 10 min.

——————————————————————————————————
8. Troubleshooting Chart
——————————————————————————————————
Problem → Likely Cause → Fix
• Dense, gummy crumb → Under-proofed; low oven spring → Extend bulk/proof; ensure oven fully preheated.  
• Spread flat loaf → Over-hydration or over-proofed → Reduce water; shorten final proof.  
• Pale crust → Insufficient caramelization → Bake longer uncovered; raise temp last 5 min.  
• Sourness too pronounced → Long warm bulk or aged starter → Shorten ferment; feed starter more frequently.  
• Weak oven spring, no ear → Scoring too shallow/deep; low gluten strength → Practice scoring angle; extra folds; use higher-protein flour.

——————————————————————————————————
9. Flavor Variations & Add-Ins
——————————————————————————————————
• Seeds: add 10–15 % toasted sesame, sunflower, pumpkin; soak (“soaker”) to prevent dryness.  
• Olives & Herbs: fold in 20 % chopped olives + 2 % rosemary during second fold.  
• Fruit & Nut: 15 % dried cranberries + 15 % walnuts; pre-soak fruit in warm water.  
• 100 % Whole Wheat: increase hydration to 85 %; perform more gentle folds.  
• Rye Blend: up to 40 % rye flour; expect stickier dough, shorter gluten strands; limit folds.

——————————————————————————————————
10. Frequently Asked Questions
——————————————————————————————————
Q: Can I speed up sourdough with commercial yeast?  
A: Yes, a “hybrid loaf” uses 0.1–0.2 % instant yeast for insurance; flavor will be slightly milder.

Q: My starter separated (hooch). Is it dead?  
A: Hooch is alcohol from hungry yeast. Stir, discard, feed. If moldy, start over.

Q: How do ambient temperatures affect timing?  
A: Rule of thumb: every 5 °C (9 °F) increase halves fermentation time. Adapt folds & proof accordingly.

Q: Can I bake straight from fridge?  
A: Yes. Cold dough is easier to score; extend covered baking by ~5 min.

Q: Why autolyse without salt?  
A: Salt tightens gluten and slows enzymes; excluding it during autolyse accelerates gluten formation and flavor precursors.

——————————————————————————————————

With patience, attention to dough temperature, and consistent starter care, homemade sourdough becomes an enjoyable ritual yielding complex, nutritious loaves. Happy baking!
